full_judgment: 2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this Rule, are that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 7 of 1984 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj against the opposite-party Nos. 2-4 for realisation of an amount of Taka 3,69,287.99 and got ex parte decree. Thereafter, the said decree was put in execution in Money Execution Case No. 10 of 1988. Accordingly, the land measuring an area of 4.17 acres of Khatian No. 67 and plot 251 of Narayanganj Municipal Holding No. 107 was attached on 29-7-89. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application under Order XXI rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure claiming their title and possession in land under attachment and prayer for release of the same from attachment. The learned Executing Court rejected the said application summarily. Against that order, the petitioner moved this revisional application before this court and obtained the present Rule. Mr M Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Executing Court has committed an error of law in rejecting the application filed by the petitioners summarily without assigning any reasons and without investigating the claim made by the petitioner. In reply to submission made by Mr Rahim, the learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that the application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code does not disclose the prima facie title and possession of the petitioner in property under attachment and, as such, the learned Executing Court rightly rejected the application.
